title: The molecular architecture of mammalian vitreous body collagen fibrils.
data_url: https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9WXP (atomic model); https://www.ebi.ac.uk/emdb/EMD-66353 plus EMD-80344..80356 and EMD-82367 (density maps)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the deposition by searching the Protein Data Bank (PDB, the archive of experimental 3D protein structures) for this paper's DOI: exactly one atomic model, 9WXP. Downloaded and parsed it (8.6 MB compressed mmCIF, 341,158 lines): 279,032 atoms, 592 chains, 30 protein entities (collagen II, V, XI, IX and opticin), 372 copies of a glucose-galactose disaccharide, 3,760 hydroxylysine (LYZ) atoms, 1,140 covalent-link records. Entity copy numbers match the paper's 8:4:4:4 stoichiometry. Also searched the Electron Microscopy Data Bank (EMDB) and found 12 maps from this citation, and searched PRIDE and ProteomeXchange (mass-spectrometry repositories) for an accompanying glycoproteomics deposit: none.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (Science, not open access, no PubMed Central copy, so no methods or data-availability statement). Resolution range 2.6-7 angstroms, the claim that the glycans mediate fibril packing and stability, and the -Gly-X-hydroxylysine- motif conservation claim all come from the abstract alone.

a1_downloadable.note: Open and immediate: downloaded PDB 9WXP (8.6 MB compressed coordinate file) with no login, and 12 EMDB maps are public.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no table and no label column anywhere. Any prediction target (e.g. 'is this hydroxylysine carrying a sugar') would have to be constructed by parsing covalent-bond records out of one coordinate file.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The deposited data is one atomic model of one fibril from one pig eye. Even counting glycan attachment sites as rows, the 372 disaccharides collapse to roughly 93 distinct sites once the four-fold symmetry copies are removed, far under the ~1,500-row bar.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not the blocker: protein sequences and 3D coordinates are present in the file, no identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed as a blocker; coordinates are in angstroms as standard for mmCIF, but there is no measurement table whose units could matter.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~9 MB coordinates; maps are a few hundred MB if needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Not the blocker. I parsed the whole coordinate file on the laptop in seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Verified and consistent: 4 copies of opticin, 4 each of the collagen V/XI and IX chains, and 24 copies each of five collagen II segments (= 8 triple helices), matching the abstract's 8:4:4:4 stoichiometry.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed as a blocker. The glycan positions are experimentally modelled into cryo-electron-microscopy density, not a model's prediction, but there is no label set to trace.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the obvious backbone for any collagen sequence task
backbone.hardware: CPU-only would suffice for the few hundred collagen sequences involved

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt (protein sequences and annotation) and AlphaFold DB (predicted structures), joinable from the collagen chain accessions in the coordinate file
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which hydroxylysines in fibrillar collagens across species carry sugars, and does that pattern explain tissue-specific fibril packing? - but this paper contributes one structure to that question, not a dataset.

controls.positive_control: None available: a single structure offers nothing to hold out.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable - no training set to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: Other collagen structures exist in the PDB (e.g. the 2025 collagen triple-helix cryo-EM work), but they are individual structures, not a comparable measurement set.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible from this deposition alone: with one fibril structure from one porcine vitreous, any model would be describing a single observation rather than learning a mapping.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use collagen protein sequence to predict which hydroxylysine residues carry a galactose-glucose sugar pair.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model a window of collagen sequence around each hydroxylysine. This paper supplies roughly 93 distinct sugar-bearing positions after removing symmetry copies - verified by parsing the coordinate file - which is nowhere near enough.
plain_idea.predict: Whether that position is glycosylated. The true answer here comes from sugar density modelled into the cryo-electron-microscopy map of one porcine vitreous fibril, so 'not glycosylated' is indistinguishable from 'not resolved'.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Matrix biologists and groups studying collagen-related eye and cartilage disease would want a site-level glycosylation predictor, but it would need a glycoproteomics dataset spanning many tissues, not a single structure.

ml_idea: The only plausible task - predicting hydroxylysine glycosylation sites from collagen sequence - would need a mass-spectrometry glycosylation dataset covering many proteins and tissues as its label source. This paper's deposition contributes a single structure that could at best serve as a hand-checkable illustration, so the project would have to be built on data from elsewhere.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not guessed: the 8.6 MB compressed coordinate file parsed in a few seconds in plain Python on the laptop. Compute was never the issue; the number of examples is.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited structures for this paper's DOI in the PDB. The answer is 1, which ends the evaluation in under five minutes.

verdict_reason: A single cryo-electron-microscopy structure, not a dataset. Fails A5 (one atomic model; about 93 distinct glycan sites after symmetry removal, against a ~1,500-row bar) and A2 (no label column exists - any target would have to be built by parsing bond records out of one coordinate file). Verified by downloading and parsing PDB 9WXP; no proteomics table accompanies it in PRIDE or ProteomeXchange. Beautiful structural biology, no machine-learning project.
